question: Indicate among the following the most probable complication that presents the patient operated on, 20 years ago, of gastric ulcer by means of antrectomy and gastrojejunostomy (Billroth II) that comes to his office referring to post-radial abdominal pain, abdominal distension, diarrhea and analytical data of malabsorption of fats and vitamin B12:

options.opd: Afferent loop syndrome with bacterial overgrowth.

analysis: The patient's symptoms of post-prandial abdominal pain, abdominal distension, diarrhea, and malabsorption of fats and vitamin B12 are indicative of a malabsorptive syndrome. Given the history of antrectomy and gastrojejunostomy (Billroth II) 20 years ago, the most probable complication in this case would be afferent loop syndrome with bacterial overgrowth. This syndrome can lead to bacterial overgrowth in the afferent loop, causing malabsorption of nutrients and subsequent symptoms.
